newsitem.title: USA: Georgia sees no GO effect from S&P upgrade to AAA.
newsitem.headline: Georgia sees no GO effect from S&P upgrade to AAA.

text.p: Georgia expects little effect on next week's $257 million general obligation bond sale from Standard & Poor's Corp's upgrade of its bond rating to AAA from AA-plus, state finance chief Weyman Smith said Wednesday.
The state already held top-flight grades from Moody's Investors Service and Fitch Investors Service, noted Smith, director of Georgia's Financing & Investment Commission.
"We basically have sold like a fairly strong triple-A for a long time so I doubt if we will see any savings," Smith said. "The bidders are going to bid probably like they always have."
He added, "We're glad to have it. It's a pride thing."
The state has two GO sales scheduled on Aug 5 by competitive bid -- a $240 million issue with maturities out to 20 years and a $16.44 million offering with maturities out to five years.
S&P upgraded the state's GO debt Tuesday, citing Georgia's strong financial position and its "improved timeliness and accuracy of budgetary and financial reporting."
Smith said there was no one factor behind the upgrade.
"The improvements were in place. It was just a matter of convincing S&P that they were real and weren't short-lived," he said.
